judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 4 Indicators (rank 0) under the same Content Standard B4.1.1.1 on quantities and place value for multi-digit whole numerals up to 100,000, within Strand 1 NUMBER / Sub-strand Counting, Representation & Cardinality. The second SFI (B4.1.1.1.2, LCs: read and write numbers in figures and in words up to 100,000) establishes fluent naming and notation of multi-digit numerals, while the first SFI (B4.1.1.1.5, LCs: round off/up/down whole numbers up to 10000 to the nearest thousands, hundreds and tens) operates on those numerals by identifying and adjusting specific place-value positions. Being able to read and write multi-digit numerals in figures is substantive support for locating the thousands/hundreds/tens digits required to round, justifying a same-rank developmental direction from the second to the first rather than mere shared-parent overlap (the nominated shared ancestry, code prefix, and generic token overlap on 'numbers'/'up' would not alone suffice). Both endpoints carry upstream audit/merge/code context and truncated source evidence, so the excerpts here are bounded; the judged relation rests on the visible statement text and Learning Components only.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are BASIC 4 Indicators (rank 0) in Strand 4: Data, Sub-strand 1 (Data Collection, Organization, Presentation, Interpretation and Analysis), so the grain and domain match. B4.4.1.1.1 asks learners to use an understanding of one-to-one correspondence to read and interpret graphs (LCs: read graphs; interpret graphs with one-to-one correspondence). B4.4.1.2.2 requires understanding of many-to-one correspondence to interpret many-to-one bar graphs (up to 4 categories) and to solve 'how many altogether', comparing, and take-apart problems (its three LCs). judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 5 (rank 1) Content Standards under the same merged Measurement Sub-Strand of Strand 3 Geometry and Measurement, so the direction rests on statement-level evidence rather than rank. B5.3.2.1 requires estimating and measuring perimeter and surface area of 2-D shapes with centimetre/metre referents (bounded source rows show estimating with cm/m referents and calculating perimeter and surface area). B5.3.2.2 extends the same measurement-with-referents reasoning into three dimensions: selecting and justifying cm3/m3 referents and determining volume of boxes by counting 1cm3 cubes. Facility with linear/square unit referents and area computation substantively supports success with cubic-unit referents and volume, a pair-specific dimensional extension rather than mere repetition, so first_to_second buildsTowards is the better-supported permitted decision over symmetric relatesTo. Confidence is tempered because source evidence for both endpoints is truncated and the second endpoint carries a same-code/different-content audit flag.
